setupSteps: Set the pulley at the top. ACE describes the attachment above head height; some sources use the highest position (snippets).

Choose the attachment. Straight bar: simplest and lets you use the most load; rope: lets you pull the ends apart at the bottom and is more comfortable for some wrists; V-bar: a short angled bar between the two. Pick the one that lets you feel the triceps most and keeps the wrists comfortable (Human Kinetics advice, snippet). Check that the clip is locked.
Choose a light weight. Pick a load you can control for 8-12 reps without swinging (MasterClass-style advice, snippet). Plate weights vary by machine and are not standardised.
Stand close. Stand about one hand-width to one foot from the stack, feet hip-width, one foot slightly forward if you like, knees soft.
Grip. Bar or V-bar: overhand (palms down), hands about shoulder-width or a little narrower. Rope: palms facing each other, thumbs on top.
Pin the elbows. Pull the attachment down to chest height, tuck the elbows against your sides, forearms about parallel to the floor (or slightly above, see Fitnessvolt vs Workout Labs).
Brace. Chest tall, ribs down, shoulders down away from the ears, wrists straight, slight forward tilt from the hips at most.
Check the view. For the camera, stand side-on to the phone so the elbow and the hip are visible.
Anchor high: door anchor on a door that closes away from you, or a sturdy post; check it before each set. Hold the band in each hand and follow the same steps.

steps.title: Take the attachment to the start
steps.action: Hold the bar, V-bar or rope, tuck elbows to your sides, forearms about parallel to the floor.
steps.feel: Light stretch at the back of the arm.
steps.visualCheck: Side: upper arm vertical, elbow near the ribs, forearm about level with the floor; front: both elbows the same width.

steps.title: Set the shoulders and trunk
steps.action: Shoulders down, chest tall, ribs down, hips still.
steps.visualCheck: Side: ears over shoulders, slight forward lean at most.

steps.title: Press down
steps.action: Straighten the elbows and push the attachment down toward your thighs; the upper arms do not move.
steps.feel: Back of the upper arm working.
steps.visualCheck: Side: elbow stays beside the ribs; hands travel down in a straight line.

steps.title: Finish with straight arms
steps.action: Press until the arms are fully straight and the hands are beside the thighs, without locking out hard or leaning on the cable. ACE says to extend fully without "locking out"; Human Kinetics suggests stopping slightly short if the elbow hurts (snippets).
steps.visualCheck: Side: arm straight, wrist straight, shoulders still. Rope version: ends split apart slightly at the bottom.

steps.title: Pause
steps.action: Squeeze the triceps for about 1 second without shrugging or leaning.
steps.feel: Strong squeeze at the back of the arm.
steps.breathing: Brief hold only; do not strain.
steps.visualCheck: Side: trunk upright, elbows still beside the ribs.

steps.title: Return under control
steps.action: Let the attachment rise slowly by bending the elbows, elbows staying at your sides, until the forearms are about parallel (elbow about 90 degrees, est.).
steps.visualCheck: Side: elbows do not move forward; the stack does not slam.

steps.title: Reset
steps.action: Pause with the cable taut, then repeat.
steps.visualCheck: Side: shoulders still low, ribs down.

commonMistakes.title: Using too heavy a load
commonMistakes.text: Using too heavy a load. Why: form breaks and the body takes over. Fix: lower the weight until all reps are strict and you can pause 1 second at the bottom.

commonMistakes.title: Elbows drifting forward or back
commonMistakes.text: Elbows drifting forward or back. Why: it creates momentum and lets the shoulders and lats help; ACE and several coaching pages call it the most common error. Fix: pin the elbows to the ribs and move only the forearms.

commonMistakes.title: Leaning over the bar
commonMistakes.text: Leaning over the bar. Why: body weight pushes the attachment, so the triceps do less. Fix: stand tall, step slightly back and lighten the load.

commonMistakes.title: Flaring the elbows out
commonMistakes.text: Flaring the elbows out. Why: shifts load to the shoulders and strains the elbow. Fix: think "elbows to ribs".

commonMistakes.title: Bending the wrists back
commonMistakes.text: Bending the wrists back. Why: excessive wrist extension can irritate wrists and forearms and often limits full extension (snippet). Fix: keep wrists straight and stacked over the forearms; try the rope or V-bar.

commonMistakes.title: Short range of motion
commonMistakes.text: Short range of motion. Why: the triceps get less work. Fix: return to about 90 degrees and press to straight arms.

commonMistakes.title: Slamming the lockout or locking hard
commonMistakes.text: Slamming the lockout or locking hard. Why: stresses the elbow. Fix: extend fully with control; stop a little short if the elbow hurts.

commonMistakes.title: Letting the stack slam on the way up
commonMistakes.text: Letting the stack slam on the way up. Why: loses control and jerks the elbow. Fix: take 2-3 seconds to return and do not rest the stack between reps.

commonMistakes.title: Shrugging or rolling the shoulders forward
commonMistakes.text: Shrugging or rolling the shoulders forward. Why: shifts work to the upper trapezius and front shoulder. Fix: keep shoulders down and still.

safetyNotes: Keep the load light enough to hold the elbows still. If you swing, lean or flare the elbows, the weight is too heavy.

Elbow and wrist caution. Pain at the back of the elbow during pushing or strengthening can point to triceps tendon irritation (snippet; clinicians often frame it as a load management problem). Wrist pain with gripping can suggest forearm overload. No pushdown-specific trial of tendinopathy was found. Lower the load, use a rope or V-bar, keep wrists straight, stop slightly short of lockout and see a clinician if pain lasts.
High blood pressure: avoid long breath-holding; stop 2-3 reps before failure.

Cable station: check the attachment is locked on, do not let go with the stack raised, return the attachment gently, keep others clear. Band at home: inspect for nicks, use a secure anchor on a door that closes away from you, and do not release a stretched band.
Gym etiquette: re-hang the attachment, wipe the handles, do not hog the cable station during long rests, do not film other members.
